data.title: S&P 500 Slips Weekly as Underwhelming Hyperscaler Results Offset Anthropic's IPO Boost
data.description:
04:45 PM EDT, 10/30/2026 (MT Newswires) -- The Standard & Poor's 500 index edged 0.6% lower this week after quarterly results from hyperscalers disappointed investors, undermining the boost to risk sentiment from Anthropic's initial public offering announcement and a pause in monetary policy.

The market benchmark ended the week at 7,580.07. The index is now down 0.9% for the quarter but up 11% this year.

Anthropic on Monday filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission for an initial public offering of Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "ANT."

The Federal Open Market Committee kept interest rates steady and said it needs more information before it can consider making a policy change. The core personal consumption expenditures price index, the Fed's preferred inflation measure, grew in line with expectations in September.

The healthcare sector in the S&P 500 had the largest percentage gain of the week, up 3.1%, followed by a gain of about 2% each in materials and utilities.

Eli Lilly's (LLY) shares jumped 11% after the healthcare giant reported a year-over-year jump in Q3 non-GAAP earnings and revenue and raised its full-year 2026 revenue outlook.

International Paper (IP) reported a stronger-than-expected swing to adjusted operating earnings in Q3, from a loss a year ago. Its shares closed up 9.6%.

S&P 500's two declining sectors this week were communication services and information technology, down 8.5% and 1.8%, respectively.

Alphabet's (GOOG, GOOGL) Q3 earnings unexpectedly declined with sales lagging as artificial-intelligence-led summaries used in search undermined Google's ( GOOG ) revenue. Class A shares fell almost 13% and class C shares declined 12%.

Reddit (RDDT) shares sank 36% after the company reported Q3 earnings that missed analyst expectations. Goldman Sachs slashed its price target on the company to $140 from $215, among several firms to make adjustments to forecasts.

Companies reporting quarterly results next week include Apple ( AAPL ) , Palantir Technologies ( PLTR ) , Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) , Arista Networks ( ANET ) , Arm (ARM), Qualcomm ( QCOM ) , Uber ( UBER ) , ConocoPhillips ( COP ) , Monster Beverage ( MNST ) , and Cloudflare ( NET ) .

Neal Truck & Bus Center, Inc.

Highway Motors, Inc. is a family-owned commercial truck dealership that has served Virginia's trucking industry since 1929. Originally established in Harrisonburg, Virginia, the company has expanded along the Interstate 81 corridor, operating locations in Harrisonburg, Roanoke, and Winchester, with an additional parts location serving the Leesburg area. Highway Motors specializes in new and pre-owned commercial trucks, including International Trucks, and provides parts, maintenance, repair, and other fleet support services to customers throughout the region. Tom Mohr, President of Highway Motors, has also been active in the industry through the Virginia Automobile Dealers Association, joining its Board of Directors in 2020.

"I first met Dan Argiro many years ago at an ATD event in Las Vegas," Tom Mohr, President of Highway Motors, Inc., shared. "From that time forward, I have seen Dan and his team at Performance Brokerage Services help other dealers around the country when they decided to sell their dealerships.

Highway Motors has been a cherished family business and an International dealership for generations. Deciding to sell was a difficult decision. I needed to better understand the buy/sell process and wanted a trusted partner with proven industry experience and expertise. From our very first conversation, right up to closing, Dan was there every step of the way. He helped guide my team and me through the complexities of the transaction, helped us assemble the right experts, and maximized our value by bringing multiple competitive buyers to the table. The right buyer is now taking the reins. We are highly confident that Korey Neal and his team at K. Neal will honor our legacy and continue serving the loyal customers of Highway Motors."

Over the last 5 years, Performance Brokerage Services has advised on the sale of nearly 450 dealerships, making it the highest volume dealership brokerage firm in North America. Dan Argiro and Pat Albero, Senior Partners of the Commercial Truck and Equipment Division for Performance Brokerage Services, were the exclusive sell-side advisors for this transaction.

"It has been an honor to represent Tom Mohr and his family legacy at Highway Motors on this transaction," said Dan Argiro. "Our teams worked tirelessly together to ensure the right buyer was taking over. Selecting Korey Neal and his team at K. Neal Truck and Bus was the right decision for Tom. Having worked with Korey on a past transaction, I've seen what comes after closing with his team at the helm. I'm confident that growth and prosperity will follow as K. Neal guides Highway Motors into the future."

Founded by Stephen W. Neal, K. Neal Truck & Bus Center, Inc. is a family-owned commercial truck and bus dealership headquartered in Hyattsville, Maryland. Following Stephen's acquisition of the business in 2006, his son, Korey Neal, assumed the role of President in 2018. Under Korey's leadership, the company has continued to expand its regional presence while investing in modern facilities and advancing technologies, including solutions that support cleaner transportation. In 2019, K. Neal was recognized by the Washington Business Journal with a Family-Owned Business Award, and Korey was named a 40 Under 40 honoree in 2020. With the acquisition of Highway Motors, Inc., K. Neal Truck & Bus Center now operates eight locations across Maryland and Virginia.

Korey Neal, CEO of K. Neal Truck & Bus Center, Inc., shared, "This is the second acquisition I have completed with Dan Argiro and his team at Performance Brokerage Services. When he reached out to present the Highway Motors opportunity, I knew what to expect from the start: honesty, integrity, transparency, and a straightforward approach to the buy-sell process. Dan lived up to my expectations. He protected confidentiality throughout the process and worked closely with my team and me to keep everything as smooth as possible at every step. We are honored to be chosen as the successor for Highway Motors and look forward to serving our new customers for many years to come. I would recommend Dan Argiro and his team to any dealer looking to buy or sell a dealership, and I look forward to our next acquisition."

Korey added, "We are thrilled to finalize this acquisition and officially welcome the Highway Motors team and customers into the K. Neal Truck & Bus family. The Mid-Atlantic is a strong economic corridor, and we see tremendous opportunity for growth and expansion here. We are fully committed to building on Highway Motors' foundation and growing our footprint across the entire region well into the future."

Highway Motors, Inc. will continue operating under its existing name at all current locations.

data.title: October ends with a thud for Intel, Reddit, AI stalwarts
data.description:
By Sinéad Carew and Chuck Mikolajczak

NEW YORK, Oct 30 (Reuters) - Monday will ring in a brand-new trading month, a prospect that appeals to many after a doozy of a last session in October.

A fresh test of this year's technology rally sent the Nasdaq composite on Friday to its biggest decline since June. Chipmaker Intel and social media firm Reddit ( RDDT ) fell 29% and Sandisk, a chipmaker that has been one of the great beneficiaries of the AI capital-spending boom, dropped 13%.

Friday's selloff came after a bruising for the big tech firms at the center of the AI buildout, led by Microsoft ( MSFT ), Meta Platforms ( META ), Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google parent Alphabet. Their shares dropped 1% to 2% on Friday following significant declines earlier in the week. 

The four so-called hyperscalers have been collectively responsible for more than a third of all the capital spending undertaken by the current constituents of the S&P 500 over the past 12 months, Capital Economics said, adding that their share seems likely to rise to an even higher level - a prospect that investors are struggling with.

"Now that the combined capital spending boom at the hyperscalers is becoming partly dependent on external financing, investors are becoming more nervous about the sums they are collectively investing and how they are doing it," said John Higgins, a markets economist at Capital Economics. 

The Nasdaq 100 index of large nonfinancial stocks fell 3.5% after being down more, putting it on the brink of a correction, referring to a 10% decline from its recent high. The Nasdaq composite is down 7.8% from its closing high, after its worst month since March 2025 wiped out a chunk of this year's AI-fueled gain.

"Investors are voting all of a sudden and all together on who will monetize the investment and who won't," said Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management. 

The damage went well beyond technology shares that until lately have ridden positive sentiment higher, reflecting a broad pullback from risk as Treasuries rallied. Silver dropped 6%, putting it down 31% for the year, and gold fell 3.5%, putting it down 10% for 2026. 

But investors said most of the selling in stocks recently is at first blush a case of 'what goes up, must come down'.

"I don't think it's a particularly troublesome leverage issue that we're dealing with. We've had such a huge move up in the whole complex," said Sahak Manuelian, managing director for global equities sales and trading at Wedbush Securities. 

Oil prices rose 2%, adding to concern about the health of a US economy that many investors see as dependent on the AI buildout for its pep. Financial stocks were hit hard, with Goldman Sachs down 4% and Jefferies off 6%. Bitcoin fell 3% after hackers took more than $6 billion from Binance. 

One question facing investors is whether a new month will mean a fresh start, after a day in which many investors headed for the hills rather than waiting to see what happens over the weekend.

"When you've had the parabolic-like moves, it makes for a very nasty downdraft," Manuelian said. "And I think that's what we're seeing. And then you have people that are starting to pull money out and going to other areas."

(Reporting by Sinead Carew, Chuck Mikolajczak and Karen Brettell in New York, editing by Colin Barr and David Gaffen)

data.title: FOREX-Yen set for third straight daily gain against dollar after BOJ holds rates
data.description:
* BOJ leaves main rate unchanged

* Yen on track for third daily gain

* Dollar index slips but on track for second monthly gain

* Euro headed for monthly loss versus dollar

(Updates headline and prices throughout, adds analyst comment)

By Amanda Cooper and Chibuike Oguh

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 30 (Reuters) - The yen was on track for a third consecutive daily gain on Friday after the Bank of Japan left rates unchanged and upgraded its inflation outlook, while declining US Treasury yields weighed on the dollar.

The BOJ left its main rate at 1.25% in a widely anticipated move, but stressed that its policy has entered a new, more hawkish phase open to raising rates once every few months.

The yen was last up 0.11% at 157.51 per dollar, but was on track for a monthly loss in October.

"The market is a little disappointed in the BOJ," said Joseph Trevisani, senior analyst at FXStreet. "The yen is a little bit stronger today but not as strong as it has been. We still have the Fed bias countering what the BOJ is doing."

The BOJ wraps up a week of central bank decisions, with the European Central Bank, the US Federal Reserve and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand all leaving interest rates unchanged as they bide their time amid stubborn inflation and tightening financial conditions.

"We think the macroeconomic backdrop will remain sufficiently constructive for the BoJ to hike in December, March and July bringing rates to 2% before taking a pause to assess the impact of tightening," said TS Lombard analyst Rory Green in an investor note.

The euro was down 0.12% at $1.1168 and was headed for a second straight monthly loss in October. It hit its lowest since May 2025 on Thursday, after the ECB left rates unchanged and indicated higher bond yields had tightened financial conditions, initially prompting traders to lower their expectations for a hike in December.

The Bank of England and the Reserve Bank of Australia will be in focus next week.

Sterling strengthened 0.15% to $1.3396. The Australian dollar strengthened 0.09% versus the greenback to $0.70345. Both currencies were on track for an October monthly gain.

AI WORRIES

When investors seek out safe-haven assets, the dollar is often a beneficiary. But on Friday the drag from a decline in Treasury yields was stronger. Results from Alphabet, Amazon ( AMZN ) and Intel ( INTC ) this week have rekindled worries about AI spending, which triggered a selloff in tech stocks on Friday.

The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against six others, was flat at 101.88. It is set for a second straight month of gains.

The euro has found some support from the pressure that the AI-led selloff has put on the dollar, but with euro zone economic growth lagging that of the United States, this strength may soon dissipate, according to Barclays currency strategist Lefteris Farmakis.

Elsewhere, bitcoin was down 2.61% to $76,780.93, as investors pulled money from digital assets, after hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in the biggest crypto heist on record.

(Reporting by Chibuike Oguh in New York; Editing by Emelia Sithole-Matarise and Nia Williams)

data.title: CANADA STOCKS-TSX posts steepest daily decline since June as gold slides
data.description:
(Updates at market close)

By Fergal Smith

TORONTO, Oct 30 (Reuters) - Canada's main stock index fell by the most in nearly six months on Friday as gold fell and investors weighed the potential impact of a pullback in AI spending on earnings growth, with technology and metal mining shares leading the declines.

The S&P/TSX Composite Index ended down 629 points, or 1.74%, at 35,620.03, its steepest decline since June 5 and the lowest closing level since October 14. For the month, the index was up 1.09% after falling 2.85% in September.

* US stocks also tumbled following disappointing quarterly results from Intel and Amazon, which amplified growing fears surrounding AI-related companies' massive spending on the nascent technology.

* "The market had been up pretty well this year on the back of earnings growth and now we're generally starting to question earnings growth as we're starting to see some scale back to the AI spend," said Greg Taylor, chief investment officer at PenderFund Capital Management. "That's starting to cause everyone to reset just their expectations of what's going to happen going forward."

* The technology sector fell 3%, with shares of e-commerce company Shopify ( SHOP ) down XX6.2%.

* The materials sector, which includes metal miners, was down 4.8% as the price of gold fell 3.5%, hitting a one-year low.

* Heavily weighted financials shed 1.6% and industrials ended 1.2% lower.

* Shares of TFI International tumbled 17.2% after the transportation and logistics company's quarterly results missed estimates.

* Domestic data was downbeat, showing that Canada's economy stalled for a second straight month in August.

* Still, investors expect the Bank of Canada to raise interest rates further by January after the central bank tightened on Wednesday for the first time in three years.

* Just two of the 10 major sector ended higher, including energy. It rose 1.7% as US crude oil futures settled 2.1% higher at $104.12 a barrel on the potential for escalation in the Iran war after the US midterm elections.

(Reporting by Fergal Smith in Toronto and Anand Gopal in Bengaluru; Editing by Jonathan Ananda and Alistair Bell)

data.title: Update: US Equity Indexes Slump as Intel's Results Trigger Sell-Off in Mega-Cap Chipmakers
data.description:
04:20 PM EDT, 10/30/2026 (MT Newswires) -- (Updates with index/price moves, macroeconomic data, company/geopolitical news from the first paragraph.)

US equity indexes sank as a sharp sell-off in heavyweight chipmakers and AI names led by Intel ( INTC ) pushed the Nasdaq Composite down 850 points.

The Nasdaq plunged 2.9% to 25,436.99, the S&P 500 slid 1.8% to 7,580.10, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.1% to 51,770.31 on Friday. Technology, industrials, and communication services led decliners while consumer staples and energy topped gainers.

The iShares PHLX Semiconductor Exchange Traded Fund, with about $48.43 billion in assets under management, plummeted 8.2%, reflecting heavy selling in AI-related firms.

Of the 20 worst-performing stocks with market capitalization exceeding $200 billion each, 19 were technology firms, according to data compiled by Finviz. Within the tech firms, most were semiconductor industry-related, led by Intel ( INTC ).

Intel's ( INTC ) Q3 revenue fell short of analyst estimates, and Q4 adjusted earnings and sales outlook lagged forecasts. Its shares plunged nearly 29%, the steepest decline on the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq. Intel ( INTC ) needs to demonstrate a "leadership roadmap" in server CPUs for a positive investor recommendation, according to a Morgan Stanley note.

Amazon.com ( AMZN ) reported a decline in Q3 earnings and a negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion, driven by investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure. Raymond James adjusted Amazon's ( AMZN ) price target to $250 from $300. Shares pared back declines, but not before hurting risk sentiment, and were still down 1.4%.

"We still expect 2026 cash CapEx of approximately $220 billion, the majority for AWS, and expect to spend meaningfully more in 2027 with a clear line of sight to attractive financial returns," Amazon ( AMZN ) Chief Executive Andy Jassy said on an earnings call late Thursday. "AWS is a $184 billion annualized revenue run-rate business, and yet the opportunity remains extraordinary."

Reddit ( RDDT ) shares sank 29% after the company reported Q3 earnings that missed analysts' expectations. BNP Paribas adjusted Reddit's ( RDDT ) price target to $110 from $180.

In geopolitical news, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said it stopped two tankers passing through the southern Strait of Hormuz and claimed that a supertanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine in the strait, Al Jazeera, a Middle Eastern broadcaster, reported. The IRGC said two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the eastern part of the waterway, according to the news report. Iran also destroyed an unmanned enemy drone craft to the east of the strait, it added.

The front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil contract climbed 1% to $103.06 per barrel, and global benchmark Brent jumped 2.4% to $117.64 per barrel.

Gold futures slumped 3.4% to $3,892.20, and silver futures plunged 5.7% to $49.38.

In economic news, the quarterly US employment cost index rose by 0.8% in Q3, as expected in a Bloomberg-compiled survey, and slower than the 0.9% gain in the previous quarter, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Friday. The Institute for Supply Management's Chicago PMI reading fell to 55.3 in October from 58.8 in September, versus the 56.0 expected in a Bloomberg-compiled poll, indicating a slower pace of expansion.

US Treasury yields fell, with the two-year yield down 6.4 basis points to 4.59% and the 10-year rate sliding six basis points to 4.93%.

data.description:
(Updates to late US afternoon)

* Intel ( INTC ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) weigh on stocks

* 10-year yield has biggest monthly fall since 2023

* Nasdaq ends more than 2% lower

By Caroline Valetkevitch and Harry Robertson

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 30 (Reuters) - US Treasuries rose on Friday, and the benchmark 10-year yield closed the month with its biggest monthly drop in nearly three years, as a sharp selloff in technology-related stocks pushed investors into the safe-haven asset.

The yield on the 10-year US Treasury was last down 36 basis points for October, most for a month since December 2023. It also had a fourth straight week of declines, its longest such stretch in a year.

The Nasdaq fell more than 2% after earnings reports from Amazon ( AMZN ) and Intel ( INTC ) rattled investors already concerned about the rising costs of the AI buildout.

The rally in US Treasuries prices in recent weeks follows a sharp selloff that pushed yields to multi-decade highs on worries about rising energy costs and rising government debt.

"The last few weeks have just been an absolute sentiment shift," said Gennadiy Goldberg, head of US rates strategy at TD Securities in New York. "The risks have really started to re-emerge, whereas a few weeks prior to that, everything was viewed as an upside risk to rates."

"To some extent, for rates investors, this is a question of whether the AI jitters persist or whether this is just a bump in the road on the way to rates remaining higher for longer."

Expectations for a December US interest rate hike remain high after the Federal Reserve this week left rates unchanged and upgraded its assessment of the economy. Rate futures are pricing in about a 70% chance of a quarter-point hike from the Fed in December, according to the CME FedWatch tool on Friday. That is down from about 78% late Thursday.

Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said on Friday the US central bank needs to raise rates at least two more times to get inflation under control.

The Fed in September raised rates for the first time in three years in an effort to combat higher inflation, tied in part to high energy prices and the AI boom.

"It's not like we think that this should be interpreted as a dovish shift," said JoAnne Bianco, partner and senior investment strategist at BondBloxx Investment Management. "We think the committee still remains prepared to tighten further if necessary. A December hike is very much on the table."

The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was last down 6.4 bps at 4.925%, and earlier hit its lowest level since mid-September. The yield on the 30-year bond was down 1.9 bps at 5.31%, and was also set for its biggest monthly drop since December 2023.

The two-year US Treasury yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, was down 8.1 bps at 4.575%. It was set for its biggest monthly fall since August 2025.

AMAZON AND INTEL SHARES BOTH FALL

Amazon's ( AMZN ) shares fell after the company reported a sharp cash outflow and another increase in spending, while chipmaker Intel ( INTC ) was down 29% after it warned that it would burn cash this year. Yields also fell on Thursday after disappointing results from top AI player Alphabet.

The Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index - the Fed's preferred inflation gauge - climbed 0.5% last month, in line with expectations, while the US economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter.

A closely watched part of the US Treasury yield curve measuring the gap between yields on two- and 10-year Treasury notes, seen as an indicator of economic expectations, was at 34.6 bps.

The breakeven rate on five-year US Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) was last at 2.461% after closing at 2.469% on Thursday.

The 10-year TIPS breakeven rate was last at 2.336%, indicating the market sees inflation averaging about 2.3% a year for the next decade.

data.title: Wall Street closes sharply lower as AI cash burn fears spark techÂ selloff
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct 30 (Reuters) - US stocks tumbled on Friday, with the Nasdaq suffering its largest one-day percentage drop since June 5 following disappointing quarterly results from Intel ( INTC ) and Amazon ( AMZN ), which amplified growing worries surrounding AI-related companies' massive spending on the nascent technology.

All three major US stock indexes slumped, with the Nasdaq sliding 2.9%. The tech-heavy index has dropped 7.8% from its all-time closing high reached on October 6.

The tech rout was sparked by disappointing quarterly results from Intel ( INTC ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) released late on Thursday. While Amazon ( AMZN ) pared losses as the session progressed, Intel ( INTC ) shares plunged 28.6%.

Chip stocks veered sharply lower, with Nvidia down 4.2% and AMD sliding 10.9%. The broader chips index shed 7.2%, slumping to a monthly loss of more than 15%. Server makers Dell and HP dropped 10.8% and 9.6%, respectively.

"It's fair to say that this week, not just today, has been very much about the future of AI and what that's going to look like, whether there will be a positive return on investment and if so, how quickly," said Oliver Pursche, senior vice president at Wealthspire Advisors in New York.

"Companies that are performing and meeting the very lofty expectations that have been set are doing well," Pursche added. "Those that are falling short and seem to be missing the mark or not executing as expected are getting punished."

All three main equity indexes closed lower on the week. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq logged monthly losses, while the Dow exited October with a gain.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 572.25 points, or 1.09%, to 51,770.31, the S&P 500 lost 140.32 points, or 1.82%, to 7,580.07 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 747.73 points, or 2.86%, to 25,437.00.

The S&P 500 tech sector posted its largest monthly percentage loss since March 2025, and communication services registered its biggest monthly drop since April 2022.

Third-quarter earnings season has passed the halfway mark, with 299 companies in the S&P 500 having reported. Of those, 82% have beaten consensus expectations, according to LSEG data.

Analysts now expect third-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth of 31.6%, year-on-year, per LSEG.

Oil supermajors Exxon Mobil and Chevron both beat quarterly profit expectations, benefiting from soaring profit margins as a result of energy supply disruptions arising from the US-Israeli war with Iran and Russia's war in Ukraine. The stocks gained 2.2% and 2.8%, respectively.

Starbucks dipped 1.8% after the coffee chain forecast an annual revenue decline due to its divestiture of its Chinese business.

Cryptocurrency-related firms Coinbase, Strategy, and Robinhood fell between 7.2% and 10.6% in the wake of reports that hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.8-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange. There were 169 new highs and 377 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 1,196 stocks rose and 3,622 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 3.03-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 43 new 52-week highs and 5 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 70 new highs and 355 new lows.

Volume on US exchanges was 19.87 billion shares, compared with the 17.26 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

(Reporting by Stephen Culp in New York; Additional reporting by Shashwat Chauhan, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Purvi Agarwal in Bengaluru; Editing by Matthew Lewis)

(Adds comments and monthly price moves)

NEW YORK, Oct 30 (Reuters) - Raw sugar futures on ICE fell on Friday, as the Brazilian real weakened and the market consolidated following three consecutive sessions of gains linked to rains in top grower Brazil. Sugar posted a 9.8% gain in October.

A weaker real encourages mills, farmers and exporters in Brazil to sell dollar-priced futures because it raises their returns in local currency terms.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar settled down 0.11 cent, or 0.6%, at 19.36 cents per lb​.

* "The trade is weighing the collapse of the Brazilian real this week against more evidence of problems with this year's production because of too much rain," said broker ADMIS in a note.

* Dealers noted heavy selling from Brazilian mills on ICE, as they lock in currency gains for their future sugar exports.

* Sugar production in Brazil's key center-south region fell 27.1% in the first half of October from a year earlier to 1.87 million metric tons, the Agriculture Ministry said on Wednesday.

* More rains are forecast for next week in Brazil, slowing the harvest, reducing the sugar content in the cane and increasing the chances of an early end to the harvest. The rains are linked to the El Nino weather pattern.

* White sugar fell 2.1% to $516.30 a ton.

COFFEE

* ICE arabica coffee futures settled up 1.75 cent, or 0.6%, at $2.872 per lb​, having hit their lowest since late September on Thursday. Arabica lost 1.2% in October.

* The market is under pressure overall from improved supplies.

* Data showed the relentless drawdown in ICE-certified stocks is starting to moderate, with bags pending grading or quality controls gaining 5% overnight to nearly 44,000 , and stocks rising 1.4% to 225,068 .

* Robusta coffee rose 0.9% to $3,204 a ton, having hit its lowest since March 2024 on Monday. Robusta lost 6% in the month.

* Robusta is also under overall pressure, with exchange stocks rising strongly and the harvest getting underway in top grower Vietnam.

COCOA

* London cocoa ​​settled down £21, or 0.5%, to £4,234 per ton, having hit a three-week low of £4,183.

* Cost-of-living pressures are a big challenge for chocolate makers Hershey and Mondelez ( MDLZ ) this year, with data from market researcher NIQ showing US consumers are so far spending less on Halloween treats than in previous years.

* Against that however, cocoa markets are expected to tighten going forward. Analysts at Expana have reduced their 2026/27 forecast for top grower Ivory Coast by 40,000 tons to 1.83 million, citing "moisture stress".

* New York cocoa was little changed at $5,453 a ton.

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: FOMC Will Need to Raise Interest Rate 'Soon' to Tame Inflation, St. Louis Fed's Musalem Says
data.description:
03:33 PM EDT, 10/30/2026 (MT Newswires) -- The Federal Reserve will likely need to tighten monetary policy "soon" to bring inflation down to its 2% target in a timely manner, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said Friday.

Earlier this week, the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee held its policy rate steady in a divided decision. The dissenters, Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, preferred a second consecutive 25-basis-point hike at the meeting, the FOMC said Wednesday.

Current monetary policy continues to be accommodative, Musalem said Friday in remarks prepared for delivery at an event in New York.

"I judge that additional firming of monetary policy will be necessary, and soon," Musalem said.

He will become an FOMC voting member in 2028.

Markets are pricing in a 70% probability that the Fed will raise interest rate by 25 basis points in December, with the remaining odds in favor of a pause, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

"The short-run economic costs of reducing inflation are less when the central bank acts before inflation has become entrenched and is expected to persist," Musalem said. "Acting sooner and incrementally now is likely to be less disruptive or costly than delaying and being forced to take large, abrupt actions later."

Inflation is elevated and broad based, with the headline and core prices continuing to run at 3% or above, Musalem said. Core inflation excludes the volatile food and energy components.

"I perceive meaningful risk that above-target inflation will persist longer than consistent with price stability," he said.

Musalem outlined two inflation scenarios for the next 18 months, with the more likely one envisaging high prices if the Fed doesn't tighten policy further, Musalem said.

However, if inflation pressures ease due to factors including lower energy prices, further policy firming won't be needed, he said, adding that such a scenario is "less likely but plausible."

The US economy remains resilient, while the labor market is "balanced around full employment," Musalem said.

"The (artificial intelligence-driven) boom in capital expenditures and wealth effects-driven consumption spending might slow from their current pace, but are likely to remain a tailwind for some time," he said. "Corporate earnings have been strong -- unusually so for this stage in the business cycle."

On Thursday, official data showed the US economy grew at an annual rate of 3.4% in the third quarter, marking the strongest growth since the same quarter of 2025, aided by robust consumer spending.

data.title: White House hearing on Fed's Cook delayed to December, Hassett says
data.description:
Oct 30 (Reuters) - The White House has delayed until December a planned hearing into allegations of mortgage fraud by Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, President Donald Trump's top economic advisor said, though lawyers for Cook on Friday declined to confirm that any date had been agreed. 

"The president has asked a small set of his people to run a completely fair process that puts all the information on the table, and then the president will decide next steps," Kevin Hassett told Bloomberg TV on Thursday. "We in the White House, the White House counsel, has worked very closely with Governor Cook's people. I think that they've agreed to a date in December to meet together and talk these things through." 

Cook's lawyer, who along with Cook herself has denied any wrongdoing and called Trump's accusations a pretense to remove her because he wants the Fed to cut rates, had previously said Cook would not be available for any hearing until after the Fed's December 8-9 policy-setting meeting. A spokeswoman for her lawyer did not confirm any new date in December. 

Trump has been trying to fire Cook for more than a year. 

The Supreme Court in June ruled that he cannot do so "at will" but that he may be able to if he gives her a chance to defend herself against any evidence he believes shows "cause" for removal. Trump announced a fresh investigation last month and initially set November 5 as a hearing date. 

Cook this week dissented on the Fed's decision to leave rates steady instead of delivering another rate hike to curb inflation, as she would have preferred. The Fed is widely expected to raise rates again in December. Trump has long railed against the Fed for not cutting rates, and accused a "political" Fed Board, which includes Cook, for keeping Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh from doing so. 

Hassett, who is on the three-person committee Trump appointed to investigate Cook and recommend if she should be fired, had called Cook "partisan" last August for not vacating her post after Trump's allegations.

On Thursday he told Bloomberg TV Thursday he feels "Chairman Warsh has done a good job of allowing, you know, normal dissent and then driving a consensus." 

The White House committee looking into Cook is comprised of "people of honor who are charged with looking at the evidence and correctly characterizing it in a way that people will be able to observe and criticize if they like," he said. 

(Reporting by Ann Saphir; Editing by Andrea Ricci)

data.title: US approves $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
data.description:
Oct 30 (Reuters) - The US State Department said on Friday it had approved the sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles to Ukraine for an estimated $2.1 billion.

Ukraine will pay for the missiles with contributions from Canada, Germany and Norway routed through the US JUMPSTART program, along with national funds financed by the European Union's Ukraine Support Loan, the State Department said in a statement. 

Lockheed Martin is the principal contractor for the sale.

President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said earlier this week that Ukraine had been waiting for almost a month for the US to sign off on critical ​missile supplies, as Russia stepped up attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure.

The Ukrainian leader has ​repeatedly called on the US, which supplies missiles purchased by ​NATO allies under a program known as PURL, to speed up deliveries ahead of winter.

data.title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in record heist blamed on North Korea
data.description:
BOSTON/SINGAPORE/PARIS, Oct 30 (Reuters) - Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a theft that analysts blamed on North Korea and said could be the largest financial heist of all time.

Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would use company funds to cover the losses. Stablecoin issuers including El Salvador-based Tether and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial froze about half of the stolen assets. 

The exchange said customer funds were safe and it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It said earlier on Friday it expected to resume withdrawal services in the next 48 hours. It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion, but Binance co-CEO Yi He said in a post on X that $3 billion represented only about 2% of the company's total user assets and public reserves. 

Binance said it had set aside around $6.34 billion of company funds internally to cover the losses. The company has a $1 billion bitcoin reserve fund designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said on X that the company owned SpaceX shares worth more than $1 billion.

Binance other co-CEO, Richard Teng, said in a post on X that the breach as a "complex attack" that was not carried out by one person and included a compromised laptop as well as malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity as it went along, "making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate."

The hackers were able to manipulate a system used to approve transactions to move money out of a Binance-controlled, internet-connected so-called "hot" wallet in a way that did not pass through normal approval controls, Teng said.

"Rest assured that we are working non-stop to resolve this, to make the users whole, and live up to your trust," Teng wrote.

'LARGEST KNOWN THEFT'

The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. 

"This incident is almost certainly the single largest known theft of any kind," British blockchain analysts Elliptic said.

The bulk of the Binance heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.

TRM said the attackers were able to order Binance wallets to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the FBI attributed to North Korea.

North Korea has ​for years ⁠used state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue, according to US and South Korean authorities as well ⁠as cybersecurity ​experts.

North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not respond to requests for comment.    

"When North Korea steals at this scale, the money supports weapons proliferation, which makes this a national security issue, not just a crypto theft," Ari Redbord, global head of policy and government affairs at TRM, said.

Binance is working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the United States Secret Service (USSS), a person familiar with the situation told Reuters.

The FBI said it was "aware of the incident and is engaged with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity, evaluate potential impacts, and coordinate appropriate investigative steps." 

The USSS said in a statement that its investigators "are working around the clock with our private-sector partners, including Circle, to identify, freeze, trace, and recover funds stolen from Binance on Thursday."

Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.

Abu Dhabi's Financial Services Regulatory Authority, which issued Binance's main operating licence, said it was "engaging closely with Binance and monitoring the incident". Abu Dhabi-backed investment group MGX declined to comment. It became a minority investor in Binance last year. 

Crypto prices fell broadly but losses were contained.

Bitcoin hit a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178 before markets stabilised. Bitcoin last stood at $77,355 and ether at $2,229. Binance's BNB token was down 6.74% over the past 24 hours at $698.

SECURITY IMPLICATIONS

Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for the crypto sector, which had already been under pressure due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.

"It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges," said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group.

Investor Michael Saylor, among Bitcoin's most prominent supporters, said in a post on X that he expected Binance to "deliver" on ensuring no customers suffered losses. "Our industry will learn from this incident, strengthen security, and emerge stronger and more resilient," he wrote on Friday. 

Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report. 

(Reporting by Tom Westbrook, Ankur Banerjee and Rae Wee in Singapore, Summer Zhen in Hong Kong, Rocky Swift in Tokyo, Vallari Srivastava and Anusha Shah in Bengaluru and Mrinmay Dey in Mexico City, Elizabeth Howcroft in Paris, Tom Wilson in London, AJ Vicens in Detroit and Lawrence Delevingne in Boston; Writing by Lawrence Delevingne, Scott Murdoch and Tom Westbrook. Editing by Stephen Coates, Mark Potter, Elisa Martinuzzi, Tommy Reggiori Wilkes and David Gaffen)

data.title: CANADA FX DEBT-Canadian dollar extends monthly gain as higher oil prices raise inflation risk
data.description:
TORONTO, Oct 30 (Reuters) - The Canadian dollar strengthened to a six-week high against its US counterpart on Friday as a jump in oil prices supported bets the Bank of Canada would tighten further, overshadowing disappointing GDP data.

The loonie was trading 0.2% higher at 1.3955 per US dollar, or 71.66 US cents, after touching its strongest intraday level since September 16 at 1.3943. For the month, the currency was on track to gain 2%, which would be its biggest monthly advance since April.

* Canada's economy stalled in August for the second straight month, while advance estimates showed GDP declining 0.1% in September and annualized third-quarter growth of 1.3%. The BoC has projected the economy growing by 2% in the third quarter.

* "Markets ignored Canadian GDP and with good reason," Derek Holt, head of capital markets economics at Scotiabank, said in a note.

* "While the figures disappointed somewhat, the BoC is forward-looking and focused upon rising inflation risk that has many complex drivers - like oil that is fired up this morning," Holt said.

* On Wednesday, the Bank of Canada hiked its key interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% and said further increases might be needed to prevent soaring energy costs from driving broader inflation.

* Investors see a roughly 50% chance the central bank tightens at its next policy decision in December and have fully discounted a move by January.

* US crude oil futures were trading 2.7% higher at $104.80 a barrel as traders braced for a potential escalation in the US-Iran conflict after the US midterm elections. Oil is one of Canada's major exports.

* Canadian bond yields eased across a steeper curve as a sharp selloff in technology-related stocks pushed investors into safe-haven assets such as US Treasuries.

* The 10-year was down 2.1 basis points at 3.780%, after earlier touching its lowest level since September 4 at 3.768%.

(Reporting by Fergal Smith; Editing by Nia Williams)
